section.sectionSummaryBrief: Just as the concept of "above without end" exists in lower worlds, so too through prayer a person can ascend from the lowest state to the highest, and contemplating his lowly state arouses in him a ratzo to escape his existence.
section.t: And behold, just as the concept of "above without end" is also in the lower worlds,
as explained above
(section 2)
that even in the creations of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah, and even in the creations of this world, the sublimity of Ein Sof shines within them,
that all worlds are incomparable and considered as nothing before Him,
and through this there occurs within them a ratzo toward Elokus,
that they desire to exit their existence,
so too is it regarding the elevation of prayer
(which is analogous to the concept of "above without end"),
that even when a person is in the lowest low, without end,
behold, through prayer he is elevated
(meaning that he is in a state of ratzo and yearning to ascend)
above and above, without end.
And as it is written,
"A ladder is set upon the earth and its head reaches the heavens," and it is stated in the Zohar,
"The ladder is prayer,"
for even when a person is at the very lowest level
("earth"),
through the ladder of prayer he reaches and ascends to the heavens.
However,
in order for him, being in a lowly state,
to be aroused with ratzo and yearning to ascend above,
he must contemplate
(not only the matters of G-d's greatness that are explained in prayer,
but also)
this very matter itself,
that he is in a lowly state.
Both regarding thought, speech, and action,
that sometimes he stumbles
(he falls through)
even in actual deed, and all the more so in speech, and certainly in thought,
and also regarding his intellect and emotions.
For although the primary service of man is to turn from evil and do good in actual deed, in thought, speech, and action,
nevertheless, this matter
(that the main thing is the actual deed)
is regarding the intention from above,
but regarding the state of the person,
since intellect and emotions are united with the soul,
and thought, speech, and action are only garments
(as explained at length in the previous maamar),
the condition of his intellect and emotions
(whether they are in holiness or the opposite)
is more significant than his thought, speech, and action.
And all the more so when he contemplates regarding his essential soul,
that even when his thought, speech, and action, and also his emotions and intellect, are in holiness, it is possible that his essential soul is in the depths of the kelipot,
as is known
regarding the statement of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai,
"I do not know on which path they are leading me,"
behold, through contemplating all this and feeling that he is in a lowly state,
he is aroused with a ratzo to exit his existence and ascend above.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The two aspects of Ein Sof—above without end and below without end—are rooted in the single power of ability, and therefore they are inter-included, as are Torah and prayer.
section.t: And behold, it was explained above
(in the previous maamar)
that the two aspects in Ein Sof
(above above without end and below below without end)
in their first root
(in the light as it is included in the Atzmus,
which is the matter of ability)
are that it is within His ability to shine and within His ability not to shine.
And since in the aspect of ability, both
(the ability to shine and the ability not to shine)
are one matter,
therefore,
even when they are drawn into revelation and thereby become two matters,
above above and below below,
they are inter-included with each other.
And so it is with Torah and prayer,
that they are inter-included with each other.
For even in Torah, which is a drawing down from above to below, there is within it the aspect of elevation from below to above,
and likewise in prayer,
which is an elevation from below to above,
there is within it also the aspect of drawing down from above to below.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The distinction between the Torah study that is drawn through human arousal and the Torah study that comes from above on its own is analogous to the difference between rain and dew, corresponding to the lower seven and the first three sefiros of Atik.
section.t: And this will be understood through what our sages said,
"In the first three hours, the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and engages in Torah,"
and the precise point of this is known,
"Anyone who reads and reviews, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him,"
and since Israel engages in Torah throughout the entire day
(one learns at this hour and another learns at that hour),
behold, the Holy One, blessed be He, also engages in Torah throughout the entire day,
and nevertheless they said that in the first three hours
(specifically)
the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and engages in Torah.
And the point of the explanation of this is,
that this—"anyone who reads and reviews, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him"—is a drawing down from above that comes through an arousal from below
(the person's engagement in Torah),
and therefore,
the drawing down is proportional to the arousal from below.
For this is what they said, "anyone who reads and reviews, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him,"
that this—that the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews—is opposite him,
according to the person's learning.
And this—that in the first three hours the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and engages in Torah—is a drawing down from above from its own side,
from a place that arousal from below does not reach there.
And this drawing down is a giving of power to the person so that he can engage in Torah, and that through his engagement in Torah the Holy One, blessed be He, will read and review opposite him.
And this is, "May my teaching drop as the rain, my speech flow as the dew,"
for the difference between dew and rain is,
that the descent of rain depends on the person's service
(as it is written,
"And it will be, if you surely listen...")
(and then specifically)
"and I will give the rain of your land"),
and dew does not depend on the person's service
(as our sages said,
"Dew is not withheld"),
for so it is in spirituality,
that rain is the drawing down that comes through arousal from below, and dew is the drawing down from above from its own side.
And the reason that Torah is compared to dew and to rain is,
because in Torah there are these two aspects.
The level of Torah that is drawn through the person's engagement in Torah—"May my teaching drop as the rain,"
and the level of Torah whose drawing down is from above
(in a manner of arousal from above from its own side)
—"my speech flow as the dew."
And this is the connection of "the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and engages in Torah" to the first three hours, because the root of rain
(matar)
is in the lower seven of Atik
[as is known regarding the matter of "sevenfold, like the light of seven days,"
that "sevenfold" is forty-nine,
and "sevenfold, like the light of seven days,"
forty-nine times seven,
has the numerical value of "geshem" (rain).
From this it is understood,
that rain is related to the seven days, which are the lower seven of Atik],
and the root of dew is in the first three of Atik.
And this is the connection of "the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and engages in Torah"
(the dew of Torah)
to the first three hours,
for the first three
[hours]
are the first three of Atik.
